notes: Correlation between forecast and realized return was negative across nearly all instruments/horizons, worsening at longer horizons for several (e.g. equities, copper). Flagged as likely a mechanical artifact of the trailing-mean estimator (regression toward the mean), not confirmed as a real reversal signal - needs dedicated follow-up before being treated as a finding.
decision: Does not clear the bar to build on. RMSE beats naive-zero in only ~20% of instrument-horizon combinations; sign agreement is near coin-flip on average and inconsistent across asset classes (near-zero on FX, mildly positive on indices/metals, negative on crypto). Treated as the expected null-hypothesis result, not a failure.
influenced_later_decisions: Establishes the baseline Model 2 (time-series) must beat out of sample, after costs, to be added.

notes: Ablation test against Model 1 on identical out-of-sample rows, not against naive-zero.
decision: Rejected. Model 2 does not clear the bar - only 15% of instrument-horizon combinations beat Model 1 on RMSE, mean sign agreement change is slightly negative (-0.007). Diagnostic confirmed the wide variation in conditioning rate (0% for Gold/EUR/GBP/crypto/MSFT vs 57-75% for AAPL/NVDA/QQQ/SPY/AUDUSD) is genuine time-varying autocorrelation, not a bug - spot-checked AAPL showed real but short-lived significant autocorrelation early in the test window that faded, and even during that real episode, conditioning on it did not reliably improve out-of-sample RMSE. Confirms: statistically detectable pattern does not imply exploitable edge.
influenced_later_decisions: Time-series momentum/reversion conditioning as designed is abandoned. Model 3 (regression/factor) is the next component to test, evaluated against Model 1 as the baseline, same as Model 2 was.
